**Standards axis — MS-279**

**Documented standards**

1. `public/shepherding-core.js:272–297` — **hard**, and it's the diff's own rule. The same commit adds to `CONTEXT.md:316`: *Hold Direction … Avoid: Comparator, operator*. Every new function then names its parameter `comparator` (`holdDirection(comparator)`, `holdDirectionWord(comparator)`, `holdDirectionHint(comparator)`, `holdScrubberLabel(comparator, shortLabel)`). The concept was just christened; the code declines to use the name. `direction` reads better and matches the helpers' own names. Pre-existing `holdSatisfies` has the same param, so this is a naming decision worth settling once rather than half-migrating.

2. `public/shepherding-dashboard.js:403` — **judgement**. `viewNewDirectionWord` / `viewNewDirectionHint` / `viewNewScrubberLabel` vs `holdDirectionWord` / `holdDirectionHint` / `holdScrubberLabel` in `shepherding-people.js:287`. Two names for the identical call. The `viewNew` prefix comes from the surrounding `newView` state, so it isn't arbitrary — but a reader grepping `holdScrubberLabel` finds one of the two copies. The new test even has to paper over it with `/[a-zA-Z]*[sS]crubberLabel\(/`, which is a tell.

3. Everything else follows house style: `node:test` + `assert`, kebab `.test.js`, source-reading assertions (45 of 132 test files already do this), the ASCII `── section ──` banners, and comments that say *why*. No `console.log`, no stray debug.

toggleHoldCmp(tagId)    { const next = this.tagHoldCmp[tagId] === 'lt' ? 'gte' : 'lt'; …

Domain audit — MS-279 (Hold Direction wording)

The code and CONTEXT.md agree on the concept and the two words. `ShepherdingCore.holdDirectionWord` (`public/shepherding-core.js:277-279`) returns `older`/`recent` from `gte`/`lt` exactly as the new **Hold Direction** entry describes (`CONTEXT.md:316-318`), and both `shepherding-people.js` and `shepherding-dashboard.html`/`.js` route through it rather than writing the phrase locally, matching the entry's "the words are always derived, never saved alongside it" claim and ADR-0011's derivation-not-denormalization stance (`docs/adr/0011-shepherding-tag-identity-and-hold-duration.md`). No contradiction with ADR-0011 or ADR-0012 — neither ADR covers direction, so nothing in them is disturbed.

One drift worth naming: CONTEXT.md's own new entry says to avoid **Comparator** as the name of this concept ("_Avoid_: Comparator, operator, at-least/less-than as UI words" — `CONTEXT.md:318`), but the code's variable and function-parameter name for the Hold Direction value is `comparator` throughout `shepherding-core.js` (e.g. `holdSatisfies(durationMs, days, comparator)`, `holdDirection(comparator)` at lines 256, 272-296), and the stored view field is `tagHoldCmp` (`shepherding-people.js:32`, `shepherding-dashboard.js:23`, `mobile/screens-shepherd.js:105`). The glossary entry is new in this diff and explicitly rules out that word, while the code the entry describes uses it as its primary internal name. This isn't new code from MS-279 — `comparator`/`tagHoldCmp` predate this change (ADR-0011's `holdSatisfies` already used `comparator`) — so it reads as the glossary drawing a line the existing code was already on the wrong side of, rather than this diff introducing the drift. Worth a call: either soften the entry's avoid-list to say "internal identifier only, never surfaced" or treat `comparator`/`Cmp` as a renaming target in a follow-up.

No inventions and no collisions found — `holdDirectionWord`, `holdDirectionHint`, `holdScrubberLabel` and `HOLD_FILTER_STOPS` are all new names that map onto Hold Direction/Hold Duration cleanly, and the test file's own framing (`test/hold-direction-wording.test.js:8-25`) uses the same vocabulary as the glossary.

**(a) Missing or partly met**

> "A selected tag chip shows the word **older** or **recent** in place of the `>` / `<` glyph, readable without hovering."
> "The saved Filtered View editor shows the same words, the same tooltips, and the same default as the People list filter."

The editor is fixed, but the saved-view **card** right beside it is not. `public/shepherding-dashboard.html:152` still prints the raw glyph for each filter tag on a saved Filtered View:

```
x-text="' · ' + (viewTagCmp(view, tagId) === 'lt' ? '<' : '>') + ShepherdingCore.formatHoldShort(...)"
```

So an elder edits a view and reads "recent", closes the dialog, and the card summarising that same view says `<3mo`. This is the exact fault the PRD names as root cause — the direction-to-word mapping written out by hand, in a third place, outside the helper. It is also unguarded: the new source test only checks the two `.js` files for the `'<' : '>'` mapping, and the "no template writes a direction phrase" test looks for the words *Held at least / Held less than*, which a bare glyph does not trip.

> "Toggling the direction on a chip does not change the chip's width."

Implemented by a fixed `min-w-[42px]` on the word span plus the chip floor at 116px, which should hold — but nothing pins it and nothing was rendered to check. Both criteria that are purely visual (this and the readable word) rest on eyeballing that has not happened here.

**(b) Scope creep**

Nothing material. `holdDirection` is exported although only the core's own three helpers call it — a small public-surface addition, harmless. The CONTEXT.md "Hold Direction" entry is documentation the project's own conventions ask for, not creep. No filter logic moved: `holdSatisfies` and `HOLD_FILTER_STOPS` are byte-identical, `test/shepherding-tags.test.js` is untouched, and all 33 tests (22 existing + 11 new) pass — so the "saved Filtered View returns the same People" and "Any/All unchanged" criteria hold.

**(c) Implemented but wrong**

Nothing. The four tooltip criteria are met and correctly routed through one helper; the default stays `gte` for absent, empty, null and unrecognised values; the idle tooltip names both directions without claiming one. The scrubber-title rewrite is behaviour-equivalent to the old `days > 0` test, because `formatHoldShort(0)` returns `''`.

**Fix**: route line 152 of `public/shepherding-dashboard.html` through `ShepherdingCore.holdDirectionWord`, and extend the glyph test to cover the HTML files.

The tag time scrubber is fixed and waiting on the merge queue. PR is [#29](https://github.com/JonathanHarris15/mosaic-website/pull/29).

The scrubber was never actually running backwards — the sums were right all along. What was wrong is that it never said which way it ran. The direction was a tiny `>` / `<` symbol you had to hover to understand, and the slider's own tooltip was frozen on "Held at least…" no matter which way you'd set it. So flip it to "less than" and the tooltip told you the opposite of what the list was showing. Correct and unreadable, which from where an elder sits looks the same as broken.

Now the symbol is a word — **older** or **recent** — and the tooltip is built from the same place that word comes from, so the two labels on one control can't contradict each other again. The default hasn't moved, so every saved view an elder has already built returns exactly the people it did yesterday.

Two things are worth knowing. The review turned up a *third* copy of that symbol I'd missed — the card that summarises a saved view sits right next to the editor, and it was still drawing the glyph by hand. You could have edited a view, read "recent", closed the dialog and seen `<3mo` on the card. Fixed, and I widened the guard test to read the page markup, not just the scripts, since that's what would have caught it the first time. And the whole suite is green: 2811 pass, with the 22 existing tests untouched.

What's left:

1. **Someone needs to look at it.** Two things I can't test — whether "older" / "recent" read well at that small size, and whether the chip really sits still when you toggle it. It should, it's pinned to a fixed width, but I haven't seen it render.
2. **A naming decision, if you want it.** The stored field is still called `tagHoldCmp` and the old code calls the value a `comparator`. I wrote the glossary to say plainly that those are just old identifiers rather than a rival name for the thing. Renaming them is a small follow-up ticket, or leave it.

Two places to look. On **People → Filters → Filter by Tags**, pick a tag and the chip now reads *older* or *recent* where the arrow used to be. Tap the word to flip it, and hover the dot underneath to see the tooltip follow. On the **Shepherd landing page**, open a saved view and hit Edit — same control, same words, and the summary line on the card above should now read something like `· older 3mo`.

Worth telling you: deploying found a second genuine bug. Two of the styling classes I used were brand new to this project, and the stylesheet is prebuilt — it only contains the classes it has seen before. So neither existed in the shipped file, meaning the chip really would have twitched when you clicked it and the hint text would have come out italic. Both fail silently, which is why the tests and the review both sailed past them. Rebuilt and pushed.

So of the two things I said needed your eye, one turned out to need a build instead. The remaining one is just taste: whether *older* and *recent* actually read well at that small size. That's what the link is for.
